transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Ramesh (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood CSM), Sofia Martinez (Endgame Head of ML), Daniel Reed (Endgame CTO), Aisha Banerjee (SRE Lead), Markus Vogel (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick sync to orient the upcoming pilot: validate latency and cost profile, confirm networking/security constraints for Private deployment (VPC/peering), discuss autoscale and fallback policies, agree on success criteria for 6-week pilot. Longer-term topics (dedicated capacity, SLA) flagged for exec follow-up.

Topics:
- Current usage and cost signal (Endgame prod vs test)
- Reliability incidents and mitigation needs (p99 spikes)
- Pilot scope: model variants, sequence length mix, KV cache enabled
- Networking & compliance: VPC peering, SOC2 artifacts, KMS for customer keys
- Next steps for benchmarks, contracts, and pilot kickoff

Transcript body (selected excerpts, auto timestamps every ~30s):
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick roll call. um we'll try to keep this tight, we have about 50 minutes.
[00:23] Sofia: hi all, Sofia here. wanted to make sure we use the time to lock down the pilot scope — team is pretty eager, cost is the main gating, then p99 latency.
[00:35] Daniel: yeah hi, quick background — we've been running an internal endpoint on 8xV100s but there's been cost and ops lift, looking at Redwood as a service-first path, need to validate both econ and reliability.
[01:05] Priya: great, thanks. can you confirm current 30-day usage numbers? tokens per month, typical seq lengths?
[01:22] Sofia: so rough numbers, 3.2M tokens month currently on staging, prod is ramping but for pilot expect 250k–1.2M tokens/week depending on rollout. Sequence mix is 60% short chat (<=128) and 40% longer completion (~512).
[01:50] Priya: perfect, that's helpful. cost-wise our estimate model shows hosted gpt-like endpoints at about $0.0012/token for the longer runs but with batching and kv-cache we can get closer to $0.0008 on average, that is with Redwood optimize suggestions.
[02:18] Aisha: we recently saw p99 jump to ~1.2s on a user-facing burst, we suspect autoscale cooldown + a bad caching warm-up. we need predictable p99 <250ms for most route-critical requests.
[02:40] Liam: ok noted. two options we typically recommend for that SLA: Dedicated capacity (reserved pools) or hybrid — pinned model on Dedicated with hosted fallbacks. Dedicated gives headroom for p99 consistency, hosted cheaper for low duty cycles.
[03:05] Daniel: procurement will push back on committed spend. Markus: are there flexible commit terms?
[03:20] Markus: hi, yes, we need month-to-month or short pilot term; long-term we'll negotiate but initial pilot can't lock us into big spends.
[03:32] Liam: understood. our pilot pricing can be no-commit for 6 weeks using burstable Dedicated with soft commit to avoid big upfronts. we'll send options.
[04:00] Priya: on benchmarks — I propose we run two bench sets: 1) a 7-day steady state 10k req/day profile to mirror expected pilot traffic, with real prompt set; 2) an artificial spike test to validate autoscale + fallback. we'll measure p50/p95/p99, cost per token, and tail latencies when kv-cache disabled vs enabled.
[04:28] Sofia: that sounds right. will share prompt set (200 queries) after meeting.
[04:40] Aisha: networking question: does Redwood support Private deployment via VPC peering and customer-managed egress? we need no public internet egress and customer KMS.
[04:58] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer KMS/HSM integrations; there are a couple of firewall egress rules and routes to be configured. we'll share a peering checklist.
[05:12] Daniel: any SOC2 / ISO docs available? we need SOC2 type II artifacts for our audit next quarter.
[05:25] Liam: yes, we will share SOC2 report and AIP security pack link. Link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-type2.pdf (note: filename in transcript, check RBC).
[05:48] Priya: small note — model selection matters for both cost and latency. for your prompt mix we recommend the 'redwood-lf-7b-q' family quantized variant for the long runs (good perf/cost tradeoff) and a smaller chat-optimized 3b for the <=128 flows. we'll include model recommendations in the benchmark doc.
[06:20] Sofia: curious about KV cache — do we need application changes? our infra team worried about cache invalidation and user-specific context.
[06:38] Priya: KV cache is transparent for prefix reuse patterns; you may need to mark ephemeral vs persistent contexts in requests. we'll provide sample SDK snippets.
[07:00] Aisha: how about rollbacks/fallbacks in case Dedicated pool fails? we can't afford user-visible downtime.
[07:14] Liam: built-in smart routing can fallback to hosted variants automatically. for pilot we can configure canary to failover to hosted model identical family; SE will show failover plan in runbook.
[07:36] Markus: legal asks — data residency: can we guarantee EU data stays in eu-west-1?
[07:49] Noah: yes, region pinning is supported for both Hosted and Dedicated; Private on-prem has options too. we'll list region safeguards and audit log retention options.
[08:05] Daniel: great. one more — encryption key control: customer KMS or Redwood-managed?
[08:18] Priya: both. for pilot if you want full control, we recommend customer KMS integration so keys never leave your account. we'll include integration notes; it's a bit more setup but gives you control for compliance.
[08:40] Sofia: ok good. on metrics — what dashboarding will the CSM provide? token-level cost, per-route latency?
[08:53] Noah: Redwood Console gives token/route breakdown, per-model latency histograms, error traces and exportable CSVs. we'll give you a 30-day demo view for trial.
[09:10] Priya: also, Optimize will recommend batch sizes and quantization settings per workload; that often yields 15–30% unit cost improvement without affecting quality.
[09:30] Daniel: any gotchas with long-context models and KV cache?
[09:45] Priya: long-context has more memory and kernel tradeoffs; the runtime chooses kernels based on seq distribution. we may experiment with 4k quantized vs 2k to hit your p99 target.
[10:10] Sofia: ok. let's talk schedule: we want to kick pilot next Monday — realistic?
[10:22] Liam: yes if we get the prompt set + network details + PO by end of week, SE can start bench harness next day. we need signature on pilot terms; we'll send the proposal template.
[10:40] Priya: technical deliverables: I'll share benchmark plan, harness code (lightweight), and runbook for failover + cache warming.
[10:55] Aisha: how about instrumentation? we'll need tracing hooks into requests for correlating user ids to traces; does Redwood provide trace IDs?
[11:10] Noah: yes, per-request tracing with optional trace ID header; Console supports distributed traces and links to token-level breakdown.
[11:30] Daniel: procurement: can we have a 6-week pilot with an opt-out at 2 weeks if metrics don't meet threshold?
[11:44] Liam: we can propose an early-exit clause in pilot contract; pricing will reflect the shorter commit but it is doable.
[12:00] Markus: sounds good. last question: if the pilot shows minor regression on quality when quantized, what's the path?
[12:12] Priya: we run evals against your prompt set, tune quantization and perhaps switch to a slightly larger model family; Optimize flags regressions and we'll roll forward/rollback per your tolerance.
[12:35] Sofia: perfect. thanks everyone.

Recap (Liam):
- Redwood to run benchmarks (Priya) and share full results by 2027-01-11.
- Redwood to send pilot pricing & contract options (Liam) by 2027-01-06.
- Endgame to provide prompt set and network details and confirm success metrics by 2027-01-07.
- Action items and owners captured in the call notes.
